avis.titre: Citrus-Floral Cleansing Oil with Gentle Emulsion and No Irritation (Ingredients Listed)Citrus-Floral Cleansing Oil with
avis.texte: YADAH’s Cactus Pore Deep Cleansing Oil is a mid-tier K-beauty oil cleanser designed to remove makeup, sunscreen, and excess sebum with a cactus-infused formula. It emulsifies quickly, rinses cleanly, and leaves skin feeling refreshed without irritation or stripping. The product arrived in a YADAH-branded green box, about 2¼ inches square and proportionally tall. Inside was a clear plastic bottle with a white pump and removable pump stop, filled with pale yellow cleansing oil. The branding feels mid-tier—neither clinical nor pop-style, but clean and functional. Ingredients are printed on the back of the box and visible in product images. The formula blends plant oils, esters, and mild exfoliants. Glycine soja (soybean) oil, macadamia seed oil, olive fruit oil, jojoba seed oil, and opuntia ficus-indica (cactus) seed oil provide emollient cleansing and skin conditioning. Ethylhexyl palmitate and caprylic/capric triglyceride offer lightweight slip and spreadability. Capryloyl salicylic acid and gluconolactone contribute gentle exfoliation, while fermented soybean extract and botanical extracts (willow bark, oregano, papaya, grape, etc.) add antioxidant and soothing benefits. Tocopherol supports antioxidant protection, and fragrance components include hexyl cinnamal and linalool. Directions advise applying to dry skin, massaging, then adding water to emulsify before rinsing with warm water. I followed the instructions and also tested on my forearm. The cleanser is pale yellow, oil

avis.titre: YADAH Cleansing Oil: An excellent performer however the real winner will be your face
avis.texte: I have incorporated the YADAH Cactus Pore Deep Cleansing Oil into my morning and evening skincare routine. I ordered it to replace my empty bottle of Pyunkang Yul PKY Deep Cleanser and to complement a recently acquired bottle of eyeNlip Eggplant Pore Cleansing Oil. All three oil based cleansers are made in South Korea. The YADAH cleansing oil like the other two oils is a gentle and effective cleansing oil. It is lightweight and smooth. It is easy to spread over my face without feeling heavy or greasy. It emulsifies quickly with water forming a milky white liquid. It rinses off quickly in the shower or wipes off cleanly with a wet towel. I have not noticed any irritation or stinging around my eyes. Of the three cleansing oils, the Pyunkang has the lightest scent, followed by the eyeNlip oil. The YADAH has a light “cactus” scent. This fragrance is exceptionally light and fades however it is unusual. It is not offensive; it is just a scent with which I am not familiar. The YADAH cleansing oil leaves my skin feeling smoother than the other two oils. The runner up being the eyeNlip cleansing oil. The external packaging of the YADAH product is distinctive, at least based on my experience. The labeling is in Korean, and the cactus green color of the box stands out. The bottle itself is functional and features a pump that dispenses the right amount of product with each use. While the packaging was not safety sealed, it appeared untampered with and seemed to be an authentic product. F

If you’ve ever wondered what it’s like to wash your face with something that smells like aloe vera's cooler cousin, this is it. The scent is oddly familiar—like that soothing stuff you slap on after a sunburn—but in a way that makes you feel like your pores are getting a spa day. This oil knows how to hustle. It breaks up makeup, grime, and whatever mystery particles the day throws at your face. Waterproof mascara? Gone. That stubborn sunscreen? Also gone. It’s like a gentle bouncer for your skin—no drama, just results. I always follow up with a moisturizing cleanser because, well, I like to double down. But even on its own, this oil does the heavy lifting. The bottle generous size means you won’t be running out anytime soon. A little goes a long way, and that’s not just a cliché—it’s math. On a final note: it’s good stuff. I’ve used it, liked it, and told others about it. If your face needs a refresh without the fuss, this one’s worth a look. Brand name: YADAH, made in KOREA.

avis.titre: Absolutely Love This! Thorough Cleaning, Beautiful Ingredients, Soft Skin SkinAbsolutely Love This! Thorough Cleaning, B
avis.texte: All I want is a deep cleaning, moisturizing cleanser that will eliminate stubborn makeup without stripping my skin. I can't believe how hard that's been to find. When I say "stubborn makeup" I mean STUBBORN. I started using false eyelashes and bonder to attach them. I have bonder remover, but sometimes it's harsh. More importantly, sometimes it doesn't work. I wanted an effective oil cleanser with phenomenal ingredients that doesn't feel greasy and leaves my skin clean and hydrated - something I can use everyday. YADAH Cactus Pore Deep Cleansing Oil works beautifully. It removes stubborn makeup including waterproof mascara and even loosens bonder (if I want it to). It leaves my skin hydrated but somehow it's not greasy and rinses thoroughly. It smells good too. It's a clean product with green tea oil, vitamin E, lactobacillus soybean ferment extract, papaya fruit extract, olive fruit oil, and more. It also contains gentle exfoliators as well but my skin feels soft and clean. There are 6.76 ounces in each bottle, and you only need a small amount. It should last for a while and considering the ingredients, it's worth the price.

I am a big fan of Korean skincare, and when I was enlightened to the existence of oil cleansers, it really changed my life. I think this one is pretty darn good, although it's not my favorite. It has a fragrance that reminds me of aloe vera or something; I assume it's supposed to elicit the idea of rubbing a cactus on your face, and I'm not sure if it's artificial or not. I used this two days in a row during my morning skincare routine prior to a gel based cleanser, toner, a gel mask, a peel off mask, eye cream/a mask to force it to absorb, and moisturizer, and I do think my skin looked bright and fresh after using this but prior to putting on the new moisturizer I'm testing, which I don't think did my pores any favors. As far as I understand it, oil cleansers can bind to oils and other impurities in your skin better than a standard gel or cream cleanser can, so using an oil cleanser as the first step of your routine helps to get you as clean as humanly possible before putting whatever other nonsense you want to on your face. I think they work really well, this one is pretty run of the mill in my opinion. I'm not sure what the exact benefits of cactus extract are, but $21 is pretty standard for this type of cleanser from a Korean brand. I had never heard of Yadah (outside of the biblical meaning) prior to trying this cleanser, but I would be interested in seeing what else they have to offer and how their products work together. Update: Added a photo of my skin a few hours aft

Feels lightweight and smooth on the skin, and works really well for everyday cleaning. It sometimes doesn’t remove heavier makeup completely, so I usually follow up with a second cleanser, but that’s easy to do. My skin feels clean without being stripped, and it layers nicely with serums and moisturizer afterward.

The moment this pale, liquid gold graced my palm, I felt a tremor of anticipation, or maybe it was just my caffeine jitters. It's got this almost impossibly light, slick texture, like trying to catch a particularly oily ghost, but in a good, non-haunting way. It smells like... well, if a cactus decided to go on a spa retreat and brought along some very fancy, slightly floral friends, that's what you'd get. Not offensive, just a subtle, "I'm here to clean your face, not assault your nostrils" kind of vibe.

avis.titre: Not for my sensitive skinNot for my sensitive skin
avis.texte: This arrived well package in well sealed. Unfortunately, most of the writing on the package is in Korean so I used a translator to read all about it.. (see pics). it has a fresh scent. There’s quite a few ingredients so I highly recommend people look at the ingredients before using if you have sensitive skin. Also note that soybean oil is the number one ingredient.. I have never used a face oil cleaner before so I have very mixed feelings about it. To me, you can feel the soy oil and it smells like oil underneath the scent. At first, I’m like this is crazy. I’m putting oil all over my face! I rubbed it for the 30 seconds like they said to do, but it never did turn color or anything like that. It just felt like oil on my face.. Washing it off was a little tricky and I have pores that clog really easy so I wanted to make sure I got it rinsed completely. At first, I was thinking that this was terrible until I dried my face and felt my face. It felt softer. This is a decent face oil but unfortunately, with my rosacea and my easily plugged pores, this is not something that I personally can continue to use long-term, but I can definitely see the appeal for others. Also, the advertisement says this helps with blackheads and things like that, but I did not notice that effect. Based on my experiences with this, value considerations ($21 at the time of order), and how I rate, this earns: 3 Stars – Average. Mostly as expected but may have issues or concerns.

avis.titre: YADAH Cactus Pore Deep Cleansing Oil | 6.76 fl oz
avis.texte: I am very pleased with the condition my skin was left in after using this cleansing oil to wash my face. My skin felt deep cleaned without any tightness. My face and neck were soft without feeling sticky or oiled up. There is a bit of a learning curve when using it as a face wash. It has a very thin consistency, and requires quite a bit of water and friction to create the emulsion effect. It doesn’t actually foam, but it does turn a milky shade when you wash with it. It is housed in a plastic pump-top bottle. The wash has a sweet, almost botanical fragrance that quickly dissipates after washing. My main issue is with how it’s so runny, it’s easy to waste quite a bit of product, especially as fast as the pump dispenses it. It’s difficult to physically get the product from one’s fingertips to one’s face without wasting any due to its water-like consistency. I do feel that, for over 20$, the quality of the pump it’s housed in could be a bit higher quality. It’s made from a very thin, clear plastic. The pump works effectively, but it requires a guard as it isn’t a self locking model. Those small, personal preference issues aside, I do think the oil cleanser itself is great. It cleans without stripping and smells great.

I have extremely sensitive skin, and this cleanser worked very well without causing any irritation. The formula is a bit runny, but it still does an excellent job of melting away makeup and excess oil while leaving my skin feeling soft and clean, not stripped or tight. I love that it’s made with cactus seed and botanical oils that nourish instead of clogging pores. It rinses off easily, has a nice light texture, and feels refreshing after each use. Overall, it's a gentle, effective cleanser, for a reasonable price, and it delivers exactly what it promises!

avis.titre: Effective, and Perfect for Mature Skin
avis.texte: I've been using this oil-based facial cleanser for a few weeks now, and I’m genuinely impressed. The texture is clear and water-light, but it lathers beautifully—something I didn’t expect from an oil-based formula. It glides on easily, removes all traces of dirt and makeup (even stubborn eye makeup), and rinses clean without leaving any greasy residue. The scent is subtle yet refreshing—a soft blend of jasmine and cactus that feels soothing rather than overpowering. What really stands out to me is how my skin feels afterward: clean, smooth, and hydrated. As someone approaching 50, finding a cleanser that doesn't strip or dry out my skin is a game-changer. I also love that the ingredient list is short and simple. No unnecessary additives—just what your skin needs. It's gentle enough for daily use, and my complexion has been noticeably calmer and more balanced since switching. Highly recommend, especially for those with mature or sensitive skin who want an effective, no-fuss cleanser that truly delivers.

I really like how this cleansing oil works. It melts away makeup , lotions and daily grime easily while also tackling excess sebum without leaving my skin feeling stripped. I also used it to take off water proof eye makeup and it worked wonderfully. The texture is lightweight and rinses off cleanly with water, so there’s no greasy residue left behind. The mix of cactus seed, macadamia integrifolia seed, and olive oils feels nourishing, and the addition of willow bark and PHA gives it a mild exfoliating boost. Cactus seed is reported to help with hydrating the skin and soothing irritation due to its anti-inflammatory properties. Macadamia integrifolia seed is reported to be a powerful moisturizer and promote healing due to its emollient properties. My skin feels smoother and refreshed after I use it, and I like that it’s gentle enough for daily cleansing. Another plus is that it’s made with naturally derived ingredients and no harsh surfactants, which makes it a good option for sensitive skin. Overall, it’s a solid K-beauty cleanser that balances effective cleansing with skin-friendly hydration.

I really love this oil cleanser. I have tried a couple and think this is my favorite. My face felt clean and felt moisturized as well. The scent was mild and ok. I have dry skin so the oil cleansers work well. The only downside is it’s very thin so it seeps through my fingers. Also it didn’t lather up the way some cleansers do. But I didn’t feel any sensitivity or redness after using and my face didn’t feel oily, so I can put up with the thin consistency

I use oil cleansers mainly for makeup removal and to take off sunscreen at the end of the day, and it works really well. I feel it’s able to cleanse my skin well enough to get everything off without needing to overly scrub, but still feels gentle on my skin. I like that it doesn’t strip away too much and my skin still feels moisturized and balanced afterwards instead of tight or dry. The texture is smooth and lightweight, which makes it easy to apply and rinse off. The smell is lightsubtle. I also like that the ingredients are simple and don’t irritate my skin. The quality feels comparable to higher-end oil cleansers I’ve tried, but at a much better value. Overall, it’s become a staple in my routine for quick, effective cleansing that keeps my skin comfortable.

I haven't used a cleansing oil before and I enjoyed the YADAH Cactus Pore Deep Cleansing Oil more than I thought I would. At first I thought it was a bit oily, but smelled good. Then I read the instructions and realized I should be adding in water and that changed the game. I found it was best to put some on my finger tips and massage into my skin. Then use my hands to add water to my face. It worked up a nice later and really did cleanse deeply. I then put warm water on a disposable face towel and washed it off my face. I used it the day after having my hair colored and it actually got off some hair dye that I didn't realize was on my skin by the hairline. Despite how clean it got my face, it felt refreshing and smooth - not harsh at all.

avis.titre: Really rinses away and leaves skin clean, not dehydrated
avis.texte: I was skeptical how an oil could help clean oily skin and clear up pores when the cause of my acne is oil... After all, oil and water don't mix, so rinsing with just water, without soap, doesn't seem like it would work. Amazingly, though, it does! It feels great, smells nice and leaves my face clean but not itchy, flaky and dry. I have no idea why this oil bonds with water and rinses away, but it really does, and since like dissolves like, it's carrying away the problematic skin oils. No acne since I started using this morning and evening, and it doesn't mean I have to choose between acne and dry skin (a lot of moisturizing lotions will trigger my acne just as badly as the natural skin oils, so that's frequently the range of options). Really happy with this!

This cleansing oil works really well for removing makeup and sunscreen without leaving that greasy film on my face. It feels lightweight and rinses off clean. The cactus seed oil gives it a nice subtle scent and makes my skin feel soft and calm after washing. I’ve been using it as the first step in my double cleanse and it does a great job melting away everything even waterproof mascara. My pores look cleaner and my skin feels balanced not stripped. A solid everyday cleansing oil that’s gentle but very effective.

I tried this cleansing oil a few times and liked how lightweight it felt. It spread easily across my skin and melted away makeup without scrubbing. My pores felt cleaner after rinsing, and it didn’t leave behind a greasy film. I liked that it rinsed off with water and didn’t require double cleansing, though it worked well that way too. The formula felt gentle and didn’t sting my eyes. I liked that it had cactus oil along with other natural oils that kept my skin feeling nourished. It didn’t cause breakouts, which sometimes happens with heavier oils. Ease of use was excellent. Just pump, massage, and rinse. Price point was fair for the size and quality. I’d call it mid-range, leaning slightly premium for a Korean cleansing oil. Overall, I thought it was effective, gentle, and a nice daily option for removing makeup and buildup.

I am impressed with the Yadah cactus deep pore clensing oil. I enjoy the light scent of the oil (light and clean). Once massaged into my skin, I add water as instructed to emulsify the oil. I can feel the difference in how clean my face feels after each use. This oil has been added to my nightly face clensing ritual. It does not take a lot of oil to get the cleansing benefit because a little goes a long way. I highly recommend the Yadah cactus deep cleaning oil.

I’ve tried a lot of cleansing oils, but this one truly stands out. The texture feels nourishing and silky, yet it rinses clean without leaving behind a greasy film. It melts away sunscreen and makeup effortlessly, making it a perfect first step in a double-cleansing routine. My skin feels balanced and refreshed afterward, never stripped. A lovely product that feels both effective and indulgent. Even the packaging is elegant and luxe!
